environmental_entry_points: tools/generate_environment_details.py delegates rain, rain_roof, all three thunder variants and all three near-strike thunder variants
processing: Per-channel DC removal, zero-phase high/low-pass filtering and gain toward prior RMS levels with a 0.65 peak cap for outdoor rain and 0.6 for the other files. Rain uses two-second equal-power tail-to-head crossfades; roof rain is low-pass filtered at 2800 Hz. Thunder uses separate recorded events, a single microphone channel per source, trimmed lead/trailing silence and edge fades, retaining the natural timing. The shared environment writer performs final DC correction and 10 ms edge fades. No synthesis, pitch shifting, time stretching, reverb or artificial stereo widening. Near-strike thunder (2026-11-01, doc 291) uses three further separate close recorded events, each starting about 0.1 s before its crack and trimmed before its rumble ends, low-passed at 9000 Hz to keep the crack, at the distant thunder's RMS target (0.057) with the same 0.6 peak cap.
